newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to privatise, liquidate 75 state farms.
newsitem.headline: Romania to privatise, liquidate 75 state farms.

text.p: Romania will liquidate or privatise 75 loss-making state farms, part of the government's drive to make the sector pay its own way and secure vital loans from the World Bank, an official said on Monday.
"We selected the 75 state-run farms by taking into account their debts, losses and area not owned by shareholders," Agriculture Ministry spokeswoman Eugenia Sendrea said.

The debts of the 75 farms succumbing to bankruptcy amounted to 1.06 trillion lei ($151.4 million), or 39.9 percent from the total losses of 2.66 trillion lei recorded by the country's state-run farms last year, she said.

The move, which coincides with a visit to Romania by World Bank President James Wolfensohn, is part of the new centrist government's restructuring of loss-making industries and an important step in winning $250 million from the World Bank under an Agriculture Structural Adjustment Loan (ASAL).

The ASAL is intended to help Romania reshape its farming sector. It includes freeing of prices, trade and the land markets and a new system of financing farming. Closure of oversized state farms is also part of the package.

The government headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea pledged to privatise or liquidate the loss-making companies inherited from the former leftist cabinet, ousted in elections last November, which halted reforms in the sector.
The 75 farms earmarked for liquidation or privatisation are located in 25 of Romania's 41 counties and account for 15.3 percent of the country's 490 state-run farms.
Ministry data showed total cropland area owned by the 75 farms amounts to 285,760 hectares.
Under a 1991 land reform, Romanian farmers got back their lands confiscated by the former communists in the 1950s.
The state farming sector now accounts for no more than 15 percent of the total. But bad management, slow reforms and lack of funds have brought the sector on the brink of collapse. ($=7,093 lei)
